clue.text: By the sound of it Richard has overcome King Edward the Tyrant

indicators.note: signals that the two pieces are to be said aloud, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: Dick, short for Richard, sits on top of a tater, as a King Edward potato is: in a down clue one word over the other

explanation.surface: A man called Richard apparently defeated a king and became a despot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Edward' looks royal but is a potato, a common variety in British shops; tater is slang for potato. DICK TATER spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant is an absolute ruler, which is what a dictator is: a direct synonym.

clue.text: Margaret discards top resembling a souffle

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is thrown away

parts.note: Peggy is a pet form of the name Margaret

explanation.surface: Margaret throws out her blouse, which looks like a puffed-up dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A souffle is made from beaten eggs, so something like one tastes or looks of egg.

clue.text: Keen old granny's first up to become ancient streaker

indicators.note: in a down clue reading upwards turns the assembled pieces backwards

parts.note: keen and avid both mean eager

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word granny's is taken

explanation.surface: An eager old grandmother jumps up and runs naked like a figure from history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the whole run AVIDOG. Lady Godiva is the legendary eleventh-century noblewoman who rode naked through Coventry.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says the noblewoman rode unclothed through Coventry, so she is a streaker from long ago: a witty description.

clue.text: Another time, second time on

parts.note: doing something another time is doing it again

explanation.surface: Doing something once more, for a second go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is the definition, as in leaning on, or against, a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaning on a wall means pressing up against it, so the preposition swaps cleanly.

clue.text: Sweet woman originally enjoyed Asian food?

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word woman is used

parts.note: having eaten something, one has enjoyed a meal; ate
rice is a staple food across Asia

explanation.surface: A sweet woman relished an oriental meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' reads as an adjective describing the woman, but it is a noun meaning dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen dessert of flavoured ice, a sorbet, is a sweet in British usage.

clue.text: Procure gas at sea for crew member

indicators.note: confused or all over the place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor is sent to obtain fuel while the ship is out on the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's officer who manages the cargo on behalf of its owner is part of the ship's company.

clue.text: Beauty squeezing nothing from a vessel

indicators.note: one piece is pressed inside the other

parts.note: Venus, goddess of love, stands for beauty
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A beautiful woman being crushed by nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Venous blood comes from the veins, which are blood vessels.

clue.text: Seasonal air producing Bacchanalian fisticuffs among the Gods?

parts.note: a ding-dong is a noisy fight or set-to
Bacchanalian revels are drunken and jolly, done merrily
the gods are the highest seats in a theatre, or heaven itself: up on high

explanation.surface: A Christmas tune portrays a drunken punch-up in the heavens.
explanation.walkthrough: Ding Dong Merrily on High is a Christmas carol. 'the Gods' is also slang for a theatre's top gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: A carol sung at Christmas is an air, or tune, belonging to the festive season.

clue.text: President has introduced his country to harm

indicators.note: one piece is brought inside the other

parts.note: Abe, Abraham Lincoln, was a US president
Lincoln's country is the US

explanation.surface: A president has brought his own nation to ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: To abuse someone is to mistreat or harm them: a verb synonym.

clue.text: Don't go for support

definitions.meaning: an appeal to remain where you are
a prop or brace, as on a mast or in a corset

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means remain, and the noun is a strut or rope holding something up.

clue.text: This is my recommendation, so drink would be drunk, say?

definitions.meaning: the phrase used when offering advice
if the letter I became the letter U, drink would turn into drunk

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes YOU as the letter U: swap I for U and DRINK becomes DRUNK.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock formula for giving advice introduces what the speaker would do in the listener's position.

clue.text: Man on a Scottish isle

parts.note: to man a post is to staff it

explanation.surface: A man stationed on an island off Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like the Isle of Man but is a verb. Staffa is an Inner Hebrides island, home of Fingal's Cave.
explanation.definitionFit: The small basalt island lies off Mull in the Inner Hebrides, Scotland.

clue.text: Loud and dark always on the ground

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical marking for loud
without light, unlit

explanation.surface: Something noisy and gloomy that never leaves the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds like the ostrich that cannot fly stay permanently earthbound.

clue.text: Fit patient in bag

parts.note: to suit is to fit or be right for
a doctor's case is a patient

explanation.surface: A healthy patient climbs inside a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A case for carrying clothes when travelling is a kind of luggage bag.

clue.text: Trudge past Ireland, land not visible in a storm

indicators.note: tossed about in a storm, the letters are scrambled
the word land is removed from the word Ireland

explanation.surface: Walking wearily along the Irish coast in bad weather with no shore in view.
explanation.walkthrough: Ireland without LAND leaves IRE; PAST plus IRE is jumbled by 'in a storm'.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to walk wearily or reluctantly, the same as trudging.

clue.text: Upside-down cakes, perhaps, upset

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is turned bottom to top, read backwards

parts.note: cakes are an example of desserts, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: Someone worried about their upside-down cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upside-down cakes' is a real dessert, but here 'Upside-down' reverses DESSERTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone upset is anxious or under strain, the adjective sense of the answer.

clue.text: See 8
African style boxing punch initially breaking limb — child's play?

indicators.note: the outer piece is split open to take the inner

parts.note: a leg is a limb

indicators.note: one piece encloses the other like a box

parts.note: an Afro is a hairstyle associated with African heritage

indicators.note: only the opening letter of punch is used

explanation.surface: A boxer with an Afro breaks someone's leg with a punch: hardly a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'African style' is the Afro hairdo; the punch's P is boxed inside it, and that sits within the limb, splitting it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The playground game of vaulting over a crouching friend is literally a children's pastime.

clue.text: One bloody series only starting up a number of programmes

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
bally is an old British euphemism for bloody

indicators.note: just the opening letter of series is used

explanation.surface: One violent TV series only beginning to air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the whole run IBALLYS. 'Bally' is a mild British swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: Syllabi are outlines or programmes of study, so plural fits plural.

clue.text: Caring but malevolent at first, contrasting case of lady

indicators.note: only the opening letter of malevolent is taken

parts.note: something contrasting is different, other

indicators.note: the outside letters of lady, its casing

explanation.surface: A woman who seems caring but is first spiteful, then the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Motherly behaviour is warm and protective, a synonym for caring.

clue.text: See 8
Realigned (right to left) 22 down for expression

indicators.note: put in a new line or order, so the letters are rearranged
R for right is changed to L for left

parts.note: the answer to the clue at 22 down, the wrap garment

explanation.surface: A phrase repositioned from one political side to the other.
explanation.walkthrough: '(right to left)' looks like a reading direction but swaps R for L, giving SALONG before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan is a catchy phrase or expression used in advertising or politics.

clue.text: Number wrapping bare middle in skirt-like garment

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a number is a song in a performance

indicators.note: the central letters of bare

explanation.surface: A dance number covering a bare midriff in a wrap skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a figure but is a song.
explanation.definitionFit: The Malay wraparound cloth worn round the waist resembles a skirt.

clue.text: Ahab hooking fishy sole trader

indicators.note: one piece catches the other inside it

parts.note: Captain Ahab of Moby-Dick hunts whales

indicators.note: suspicious or odd, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Captain Ahab lands a suspicious sole and sells it.
explanation.definitionFit: A wholesaler buys goods in bulk and sells them on to retailers: a kind of trader.

clue.text: Brownish-yellow shine

definitions.meaning: to ... something is to polish it

explanation.definitionFit: The colour of undyed leather, and the verb for rubbing to a gloss.

clue.text: Animal biting 'umongous elephant's head in adventure story

indicators.note: one piece takes the other into its mouth, inside

parts.note: a beast is an animal
humongous spoken without its H means huge, here huge without its H

indicators.note: the first letter of elephant's

explanation.surface: A creature chomping on a huge elephant's head in an adventure.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of ''umongous' tells you to drop H from HUGE too. Beau Geste is P. C. Wren's Foreign Legion novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1924 novel about the French Foreign Legion is a classic adventure tale.

clue.text: See 24 down
Stop a bird (tail first) that's 13

definitions.note: a house without flights of stairs

parts.note: a bung is a stopper

indicators.note: the last letter is moved to the front

parts.note: an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: Plug up a bird, rear end first.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 down is read as 'without flights', meaning no flights of stairs, not unable to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-storey house has no staircase, so no flights of steps.
